status.statement: A draft specification and three machine-readable capability contracts. The contracts were re-read from disk during this build and every operation they declare was matched against the operation tables in the spec; the spec's own structure was recounted from the file.
status.source: build-site.mjs on 2026-08-17: it parses docs/spec/README.md with fenced code blocks stripped, counts its numbered headings, its task boxes and its acceptance criteria, and compares the operation tables in §8 against records/contracts/*.contract.json — which are byte-identical copies of the files in AmpersandBoxDesign/contracts/v0.1.0/, checked by SHA-256 on every build run in the portfolio tree.
status.limit: This establishes that a document exists and that it does not contradict the contract files beside it. It does not establish that any of it works. Nothing here has been compiled, benchmarked, deployed or used: the delta-CRDT convergence claim, the federated-learning privacy claim, the 15% route improvement and every latency figure in the spec are design intentions written down, not measurements. The spec's own Pre-Phase exists precisely because those assumptions are unvalidated, and it has not been started.

advance.requires: A mix project in this repository whose test suite runs. The nearest honest step is the spec's own FV-1 — a minimal epoch-aware delta-CRDT for position, heading and speed, driven through simulated partitions until it either converges within the stated window or does not. One feasibility validation with a result would move this rung; a hundred more pages of specification would not.

artifacts.name: The v0.1 draft specification
artifacts.detail: Seventeen numbered sections covering spatial digital twins as delta-CRDTs, federated route learning over LoRA adapters, GNN route optimization, a geofencing engine, an OTP supervision tree, a data model and a 34-week roadmap. It is a design document with Elixir type declarations in it, not Elixir.
artifacts.witness: The file, re-read and recounted by this build. Every § number cited on this page was resolved against its real headings, with fenced code blocks stripped first.

artifacts.name: Three &space capability contracts
artifacts.detail: &space.fleet, &space.route and &space.geofence as JSON: named operations with typed input and output slots, the primitives they accept from and feed into, and their A2A skill names. A declaration a client could be written against — not a service a client can call.
artifacts.witness: Byte-identical copies of AmpersandBoxDesign/contracts/v0.1.0/, compared by SHA-256 during this build. Every operation they name was matched against the tables in §8 of the spec.

artifacts.name: The PULSE loop manifest
artifacts.detail: A five-phase loop — retrieve_twin, route_inference, act_dispatch, learn_outcome, consolidate_twin — declared in prose, with its closure, cadence, substrates and cross-loop signals. Every phase maps to one of PULSE's five canonical kinds.
artifacts.witness: Extracted from the spec by this build. It is prose in a Markdown table: no geofleetic.spatial_intelligence.pulse.json exists in PULSE/manifests/, so nothing can validate it against the PULSE v0.1 schema.

unmeasured.name: FV-1 — delta-CRDT convergence
unmeasured.detail: The spec's own first feasibility validation: prototype a minimal position/heading/speed delta-CRDT, drive a hundred concurrent twin updates through delayed and reordered messages, and check that state converges within five seconds of the partition healing with no lost updates. Everything else in the document assumes this holds.
unmeasured.needs: A mix project and a few hundred lines of Elixir. This is the cheapest real result available here.

unmeasured.name: FV-2 — federated learning without EXLA
unmeasured.detail: Train a LoRA adapter on synthetic routes with Nx and ONNX only, then check that extracting, compressing and aggregating the deltas produces a merged adapter within five percent of a centrally-trained baseline. The privacy argument this whole product rests on is worth nothing if the merged model is worse than useless.
unmeasured.needs: A training loop, a synthetic route set, and a baseline to lose to.

unmeasured.name: FV-3 — a GNN that runs on the BEAM
unmeasured.detail: Whether Nx can express a graph network for route scoring at all, and at what latency on a fifty-node road graph. The spec carries its own escape hatch — a Python sidecar — and marks the outcome as a decision gate that would rewrite the technology stack and the supervision tree.
unmeasured.needs: A benchmark, and a willingness to publish the number if it is bad.

unmeasured.name: Any implementation at all
unmeasured.detail: No mix project, no supervision tree, no MCP server, no PostGIS migration, no Tile38 client. The eight MCP tools named in §9.2 do not exist as code anywhere; the eight names are the whole of them.
unmeasured.needs: Phase 0 of the roadmap, which is scheduled after a Pre-Phase that has not begun.

unmeasured.name: Anyone else implementing these contracts
unmeasured.detail: A capability contract is only worth something when two parties written by different people agree on it. One unimplemented contract cannot demonstrate that; it can only fail to be contradicted.
unmeasured.needs: A provider or a consumer of &space.fleet that we did not write.
